Just hours after announcing Apple would support communities affected by wildfires in Southern Europe, Cook said the company would also donate funds to assist rescue efforts for the earthquake in Kumamoto, Japan. Details are below.

Apple to Donate Funds to Assist Rescue Efforts in Japan

Apple CEO Cook once again announced Apple's plans to assist communities affected by natural disasters on the X platform.

Cook said the company was making a donation to support rescue efforts in Japan, adding that the country "holds a very special place in his heart." You can see his full post below:

On Tuesday afternoon, a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan, with the epicenter located about 12 miles south of Kumamoto City. So far, 34 people have died, thousands have been forced to evacuate, and tens of thousands of households remain without water and power.

According to Reuters, continuous aftershocks and extreme heat in the area are also making rescue and recovery efforts more difficult.

Cook's announcement came just hours after he said Apple would assist millions of wildfire victims in Southern Europe, continuing Apple's tradition of stepping up during natural disasters and other emergencies.

Apple also has an internal donation program called "Employee Giving," which has raised over US$880 million to date through a matching gift policy.
